title: Twelve Feasts and One Cold Plate
subtitle: 饮食文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食文化（历史社会与文化·饮食文化）
meta: 主题语境：饮食文化（历史社会与文化·饮食文化）　|　核心词汇：dessert　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dessert 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 my grandmother ① served a dessert that no cook in the town would have attempted, and she said the serving was the whole of the feast. The ② dessert, meaning the sweet dish and not the course, ran twelve feasts and stayed untasted by the children; a dessert, she said, is the only thing at a table that is judged by how long it is left uncut.

Every ③ dessert in that house had the same cold plate under it, and the ④ dessert at the end, meaning the one she kept for the guests and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked for twice. A dessert, my aunt said, is nine parts sugar and one part somebody willing to wait; my grandmother said the waiting is the part that fills twelve feasts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dessert was the whole of the dinner, meaning the course and not the sweet dish. The ⑥ dessert, meaning the course and not any of that, is the only thing at a dinner that everybody praises and nobody finishes; dessert, he said, is either something you serve or the only word that means both a sweet dish and a course. He said the course is the part they remember.

By 1955 the ⑦ dessert had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the cold plate. The ⑧ dessert of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in December, was one house and twelve feasts of waiting; dessert, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wait. She said the waiting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dessert I remember is the one at the end, which was served in 1969 and is still described as the strangest in the house. A ⑩ dessert, my aunt said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being waited for; every dessert, she said, is a course that has agreed to look like a sweet dish. She said the course was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 甜点；甜食（指端上桌的那一份）
B. n. 甜点（指那份甜食本身，与那道程序相对）
C. 固定搭配：serve a dessert 端上一份甜点
D. n. 甜点（指留给客人用的那一份）
E. n. 甜点；餐后甜食（抽象总称，指一屋子人的餐后之甜）
F. n. 甜点（指菜单上写到、被列名的那一份）
G. n. （餐后）甜点这道程序（指宴席上的最后一道）
H. n. 最后一道（抽象总称，指人人称赞却无人吃完的那道）

items.q: served a dessert that no cook in the town would have attempted
The dessert, meaning the sweet dish and not the course
the dessert was the whole of the dinner
the dessert had become a line in a menu
The dessert of the whole thing
A dessert, my aunt said in 1971

answers.why: serve a dessert 意为“端上一份甜点”，1946 年祖母端上了一份全镇没有一位厨子敢尝试的甜点。
dessert 意为“甜点”，指那份甜食本身而不是那道程序，它历经十二次宴席而孩子们始终没尝到。
dessert 意为“甜点”，指那栋房子里每一份甜点，每一份下面都垫着同一只冷盘子。
dessert 意为“甜点”，指留给客人用的那一份，是唯一有人要过两次的。
dessert 意为“餐后甜点这道程序”，指宴席上的最后一道，叔叔说这道程序就是那顿饭的全部。
dessert 意为“最后一道”，指人人称赞却无人吃完的那道而不是那份甜食，是饭桌上人人都称赞、却无人吃完的东西。
dessert 意为“甜点”，指菜单上写到、被列名的那一份，到 1955 年这份甜点成了菜单里的一行。
dessert 意为“甜点、餐后甜食”，祖母十二月写道，整件事的餐后之甜是一栋房子和十二次宴席的等待。
dessert 意为“甜点”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1969 年端上桌，至今仍被说成屋里最奇的一份。
dessert 为抽象总称，姑姑 1971 年说，一份甜点是唯一会因为被等待而变得更好的东西。
